screen1-a1.glyph: gold crown with a red jewel
screen1-a1.description: gold crown picture in the top bar, left of the gear
screen1-a1.location: top right, first of two pictures
screen1-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: resource_id iv_premium told me to watch for a premium/subscription page; no content_desc or talkback label exists; not used in the verdict
screen1-a1.convention_relied_on: a crown is used by some freemium apps to mark a paid tier, but it is not an established convention a first-time user of mobile apps would read as an action — my reading, confidence medium
screen1-a1.initial_rationale: no word anywhere near it, and a crown is decoration or a brand mark to a first-time user rather than a known control glyph

test_cases.precondition: app open on the home screen (live app matches the capture: no file access granted, "To continue, please allow file access on your device." empty state)
test_cases.action: focus/long-press the crown to look for a tooltip or label, then tap it once and watch what opens
test_cases.expected_result: if a label, tooltip or caption appears on press, or the page it opens is plainly what a crown promises, the verdict changes
test_cases.confirms_if: no label or tooltip in any state, and the page it opens is not predictable from a crown
test_cases.overturns_if: a label/tooltip appears, or the outcome is what a first-time user would predict from the glyph
test_cases.observed_result: no label or tooltip appeared on press; the tap opened a full-screen subscription offer "Try the Premium plan completely free" with a "Start Free Trial" button and "3 day free trial, then $29.99/year" — nothing on the home screen said the crown leads to a paid-plan offer

screen1-a1.deciding_evidence: no visible label in any state; the crown opened a paid subscription offer, which nothing on the screen announced
screen1-a1.recommendation: add a visible caption such as "Premium" (or "Go Premium") under or beside the crown

screen1-a2.glyph: gear with a wrench laid across it
screen1-a2.description: gear with a wrench laid across it, top bar far right
screen1-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: resource_id iv_setting told me to watch for a Settings page; no content_desc or talkback label; not used in the verdict
screen1-a2.convention_relied_on: gear = settings, an established mobile convention (the wrench overlay does not change the reading) — my reading, confidence high
screen1-a2.initial_rationale: unlabeled, but a gear is a widely known settings convention — common-icon exemption pending the behavioural test

test_cases.precondition: app open on the home screen (live app matches the capture: no file access granted, "To continue, please allow file access on your device." empty state)
test_cases.expected_result: a settings page opens
test_cases.confirms_if: it opens something other than settings, making the convention misleading
test_cases.overturns_if: it opens a settings page
test_cases.observed_result: a page titled "Settings" opened with Keep screen on, Language, Set default reader, Add widget, Rate App, Share App, Privacy Policy, Terms of Use rows

screen1-a2.deciding_evidence: the gear opened the Settings page, exactly as the gear convention promises

screen1-a3.description: pill-shaped chip reading "PDF" in the file-type row under the title (drawn as the current/selected item; tapping the current item changes nothing but the item carries the selected state, so it stays in scope)
screen1-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "PDF" repeats the visible word; not used in the verdict
screen1-a3.initial_rationale: "PDF" is a widely known document type; in a row of file types on a document reader the chip reads as "show PDF files", and the filled chip shows which is current

test_cases.precondition: app open on the home screen (live app matches the capture: no file access granted, "To continue, please allow file access on your device." empty state)
test_cases.expected_result: the PDF chip becomes the selected one and the list area switches to PDF documents
test_cases.confirms_if: the chip does something other than switch the file type
test_cases.overturns_if: the chip switches the selected file type
test_cases.observed_result: the PDF chip became the filled/selected chip and the content area showed the same no-file-access empty state (no files can be listed without access) — consistent with a file-type filter

screen1-a3.deciding_evidence: the tap switched the selected file type to PDF, as the word on it predicts

test_cases.precondition: HWP chip already selected
test_cases.expected_result: nothing further happens

screen1-a11.glyph: white corner brackets with a horizontal line through the middle, on a black circle
screen1-a11.description: round black floating button with white corner brackets and a line through the middle
screen1-a11.location: lower right, above the bottom bar
screen1-a11.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Scan to PDF" told me to watch for a scanner; not used in the verdict
screen1-a11.convention_relied_on: four corner brackets with a line across = viewfinder / scan (QR or document) — an established scanning convention, my reading, confidence medium
screen1-a11.initial_rationale: unlabeled; the viewfinder glyph conventionally means "scan" — common-icon exemption pending the behavioural test

test_cases.precondition: app open on the home screen (live app matches the capture: no file access granted, "To continue, please allow file access on your device." empty state)
test_cases.action: tap the round button and observe (do not grant any permission)
test_cases.expected_result: a scanner / camera view opens
test_cases.confirms_if: it does something other than open a scanner
test_cases.overturns_if: a scanning screen opens, matching the viewfinder convention
test_cases.observed_result: no scanner opened: a dialog "Request permission to access all files — To read and edit your document files, please allow \"PDF Reader, PDF Viewer\" to access all your files." with a single "GO TO SET" button appeared; nothing mentioned scanning; dismissed with Back

screen1-a11.deciding_evidence: the viewfinder glyph promised scanning but the tap produced an all-files permission request that never mentions scanning, so neither the glyph nor its result tells the user what the button does
screen1-a11.recommendation: give the button a visible label such as "Scan to PDF" (an extended floating button), and if file access is a prerequisite say so in the prompt ("To save scans, allow file access")

screen7-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: resource_id iv_premium told me to watch for a premium/subscription page; no content_desc or talkback label exists; not used in the verdict
screen7-a1.convention_relied_on: a crown is used by some freemium apps to mark a paid tier, but it is not an established convention a first-time user of mobile apps would read as an action — my reading, confidence medium
screen7-a1.initial_rationale: no word anywhere near it, and a crown is decoration or a brand mark to a first-time user rather than a known control glyph
screen7-a1.deciding_evidence: no visible label in any state; the crown opened a paid subscription offer, which nothing on the screen announced — tested once on screen1-a1; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here
screen7-a1.recommendation: add a visible caption such as "Premium" (or "Go Premium") under or beside the crown

screen7-a2.glyph: gear with a wrench laid across it
screen7-a2.description: gear with a wrench laid across it, top bar far right
screen7-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: resource_id iv_setting told me to watch for a Settings page; no content_desc or talkback label; not used in the verdict
screen7-a2.convention_relied_on: gear = settings, an established mobile convention (the wrench overlay does not change the reading) — my reading, confidence high
screen7-a2.initial_rationale: unlabeled, but a gear is a widely known settings convention — common-icon exemption pending the behavioural test
screen7-a2.deciding_evidence: the gear opened the Settings page, exactly as the gear convention promises — tested once on screen1-a2; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here

screen7-a3.description: pill-shaped chip reading "PDF" in the file-type row under the title
screen7-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "PDF" repeats the visible word; not used in the verdict
screen7-a3.initial_rationale: "PDF" is a widely known document type; in a row of file types on a document reader the chip reads as "show PDF files", and the filled chip shows which is current
screen7-a3.deciding_evidence: the tap switched the selected file type to PDF, as the word on it predicts — tested once on screen1-a3; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here

screen7-a4.description: pill-shaped chip reading "HWP" in the file-type row under the title
screen7-a4.location: top, second chip in the row
screen7-a4.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "HWP" repeats the visible word; not used in the verdict
screen7-a4.initial_rationale: "HWP" is a file-format abbreviation (a Korean word-processor format) that a first-time user outside that market will not recognise; next to PDF/Word/Excel/PPT it reads as a file type, but nothing says which files or what pressing it changes
screen7-a4.deciding_evidence: pressing it only recoloured the chip; neither the chip nor the result ever says what "HWP" is — tested once on screen1-a4; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here
screen7-a4.recommendation: spell out the format, e.g. "Hangul (HWP)" or "HWP documents", or drop the chip in locales where the format is not used

screen35-a1.convention_relied_on: a crown is used by some freemium apps to mark a paid tier, but it is not an established convention a first-time user of mobile apps would read as an action — my reading, confidence medium
screen35-a1.initial_rationale: no word anywhere near it, and a crown is decoration or a brand mark to a first-time user rather than a known control glyph
screen35-a1.deciding_evidence: no visible label in any state; the crown opened a paid subscription offer, which nothing on the screen announced — tested once on screen1-a1; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here
screen35-a1.recommendation: add a visible caption such as "Premium" (or "Go Premium") under or beside the crown

screen35-a2.glyph: gear with a wrench laid across it
screen35-a2.description: gear with a wrench laid across it, top bar far right
screen35-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: resource_id iv_setting told me to watch for a Settings page; no content_desc or talkback label; not used in the verdict
screen35-a2.convention_relied_on: gear = settings, an established mobile convention (the wrench overlay does not change the reading) — my reading, confidence high
screen35-a2.initial_rationale: unlabeled, but a gear is a widely known settings convention — common-icon exemption pending the behavioural test
screen35-a2.deciding_evidence: the gear opened the Settings page, exactly as the gear convention promises — tested once on screen1-a2; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here

screen35-a3.description: pill-shaped chip reading "PDF" in the file-type row under the title (drawn as the current/selected item; tapping the current item changes nothing but the item carries the selected state, so it stays in scope)
screen35-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "PDF" repeats the visible word; not used in the verdict
screen35-a3.initial_rationale: "PDF" is a widely known document type; in a row of file types on a document reader the chip reads as "show PDF files", and the filled chip shows which is current
screen35-a3.deciding_evidence: the tap switched the selected file type to PDF, as the word on it predicts — tested once on screen1-a3; this is a duplicate of that control and the verdict is carried here

screen35-a4.description: pill-shaped chip reading "HWP" in the file-type row under the title
screen35-a4.location: top, second chip in the row
screen35-a4.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "HWP" repeats the visible word; not used in the verdict

persona_issue_classifications.basis: Gopal (navigate with difficulty, opinion softened): cue "The cog wheel looks something like the settings picture on my own telephone, but the spanner across it makes it a different picture from the one I know."; why "A plain cog I might recognise; this one has something added to it, and there is no word, so I am not certain enough to trust it."; solution "Write the word 'Settings' under it, and use the same plain cog as the rest of my telephone."; after testing: "The cog led to a page plainly headed 'Settings', and 'Tools' led somewhere quite different. So pressing it is safe and the heading tells me where I am once I arrive. I still could not be sure before pressing, because the picture has a spanner added and no word, so it remains a small difficulty rather than none." | Kwame (navigate with difficulty, opinion softened): cue "Only the picture. The cog suggests settings; the spanner suggests tools, and there is also a 'Tools' tab at the bottom, so the picture points two ways."; why "The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom. I cannot decide which one this is without pressing it, and I would read the screen over and over trying to settle it."; solution "Write 'Settings' under it, and use a plain cog without the spanner so it cannot be confused with 'Tools'."; after testing: "The cog opens a page plainly titled 'Settings', and the Tools tab opens a different page of tools, so they are not the same place. My trouble was before pressing: the picture mixes a cog and a spanner, and the answer only came from trying it. A plain cog or the word 'Settings' would settle it." — the cue names a picture that was there but could be read two ways (settings or tools); the fix asked is to plain the picture and word it
persona_issue_classifications.note: classification only; my own verdict is unchanged and the disagreement stands
